newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina recalls envoy in trade dispute - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina recalls envoy in trade dispute - report.

text.p: The Argentine ambassador to Brazil has been recalled to Buenos Aires to explain his harsh criticism of a Brazilian official, a local newspaper reported on Sunday.

Ambassador Diego Guelar last week blasted Brazil's Central Bank Director of International Affairs Gustavo Franco over Brasilia having changed its import financing rules at the end of March without warning its Mercosur trade bloc partners.
"I think you can call it treason," he was quoted as saying in Brazil after Franco announced the measures.
The Argentine daily La Nacion said on Sunday that Guelar had sent a formal apology to Franco.
No foreign ministry official could be immediately reached for comment.
Brasilia two weeks ago restricted short-term import financing of less than 360 days, effectively forcing importers to pay in cash.
But under pressure from its Mercosur partners Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay and their free trade associates Bolivia and Chile, Brazil later agreed to give the bloc a partial exemption for 120 days.
Brazil also agreed to inform its partners in advance of any such measures in the future.
In an interview with La Nacion, Guelar also blamed the Brazilian media for taking advantage of his difficulty speaking Portuguese to misquote him.
La Nacion said Brazilian authorities had not asked for Guelar's replacement over the incident, as had been reported by Brazilian media.
